# F-star residue class (iii): the entry-class scope of Lemma AN/MX — mis-stated and empty (no kappa)

## Scope

Kappa-blocker **KB5d** (explicit open request; scope changed from the drawn card and recorded in `TASK.json`): settle the **statement** of residue class **(iii) "non-dyadic entries"** of open problem **F-star** of the merged `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas` package ([PR 1590](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1590) by DreamingOfClouds, with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code assistance): `cert(M) >= floor(2v/3)` for every exact 3-total rational decoder `M = sum_j p_j q_j^T`. [PR 2717](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2717) by Aaron Wang (navinor) demoted exactly: "(c) for non-dyadic entries (odd primes in denominators) the mod-2 anchor does not apply at all". [PR 2747](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2747) by Aaron Wang (navinor) closed class (i) on the fixtures with Lemma MX and left class (iii) untouched. [PR 2774](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2774) by Aaron Wang (navinor) recorded class (iii) as mathematically murky: odd-denominator rationals are 2-integral, so Lemma AN's mod-2 anchor may already cover them. This PR settles the statement. Package `research/fstar-entry-class-scope-seed63d5f999/`. **F-star itself is not proved and not refuted here; no kappa, supplier or frontier change is claimed.**

Agent: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent human review claimed). Base `544a7e82810e30cab61c297cb2e2ea86127fe944` (frozen assignment pin; canonical main fetched at `66bb142b233f95399922c9e1894a4b5ef850bf40` at the pre-submission refresh, with the pinned inputs `research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas/README.md` and `docs/research/agent-task-catalog.json` unchanged between the two; priority revision 5).

## The precise entry-class statement (PROVEN)

For a fixed factorization `M = sum_{j=1..3} p_j q_j^T`, let `m_j = min_t v_2(p_j(t))`, `n_j = min_s v_2(q_j(s))` (nonzero entries), `c_j = m_j + n_j`, and `gamma = min_j c_j`. Here `v_2` is the 2-adic valuation, `Z_(2)` is the ring of odd-denominator rationals, and `Z[1/2]` the dyadic rationals.

**Lemma SC (exact scope of Lemma AN's hypothesis).** `c_j` is the 2-adic content of the rank-1 matrix `p_j q_j^T`, invariant under per-total rescaling; the factorization becomes 2-integral after per-total powers of two **if and only if** `c_j >= 0` for every total. Hence: entries in `Z_(2)` (odd denominators — this is exactly the "non-dyadic" class of the demoted claim (c)) satisfy Lemma AN's hypothesis verbatim, with no rescaling; entries in `Z[1/2]` (dyadic) satisfy it exactly when all `c_j >= 0` — dyadic entryhood alone does not imply it; general `Q` is governed by the same per-total criterion.

**Lemma SG (scale-invariant anchor; exact reach).** For every rational factorization of every entry class, one global rescaling `M -> 2^{-gamma} M` makes Lemma AN applicable; the reduced labels satisfy `K_ts = 2^{-gamma} M_ts mod 2`, so `K_ts = 0` at every incidence and `K_tt = 1` exactly on `S_gamma = {t : v_2(M_tt) = gamma}`. Therefore `cert(M) >= |S_gamma|`, and the reach is exact: `v_2(M_tt) >= gamma` always, and no mod-2 anchor from any power-of-two normalization of the given factorization anchors a line outside `S_gamma`. Lemma AN's count `#{t : M_tt odd}` is the special case `gamma = 0`; PR 2717's corollary sentence about dyadic decoders has a normalization gap as literally stated (control SC1), which Lemma SG repairs for all rational decoders: F-star holds whenever at most `floor(v/3)` lines have `v_2(M_tt) > gamma` (the cancellation lines).

**Pattern invariance (the collapse).** `lambda M` shares `(pi, sigma, Z)` with `M`, hence `cert` and every chain cost `cost(B)` are invariant under global rescaling, and every rational pattern has an integer-entry realization (scale each total by the lcm of all denominators). The realizable patterns are identical over `Z`, `Z[1/2]`, `Z_(2)` and `Q`, so F-star holds for all rational decoders if and only if it holds for integer-entry decoders. **No residue of F-star can live in entry denominators: class (iii) is empty as an obstruction.** Lemmas SF/MP/RK are coefficient-free; Lemma MX's `A`/`U` parts use the anchor labels (available everywhere by Lemma SG, with `A` inside `S_gamma`) and its `T` part is coefficient-free, so none of the four lemmas carries an entry-denominator restriction. The only "if and only if" statements are Lemma SC's and Lemma SG's reach, both proved in both directions; no other necessity claim is made.

## Smallest-first falsifier search (CHECKED, scoped negative)

Smallest falsifying instance first, `v` ascending from 3, three families aimed at the audited statement; falsifier criterion an explicit admissible pairing `B` with chain cost below `floor(2v/3)` or exact `cert` below threshold; an instance is *certified* once a machine-checked L8 witness at or above threshold is replayed.

| family | entries | instances | class | Lemma AN hypothesis | falsifiers | certified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evenden` | halves, quarters | 28 | dyadic | fails on 28 (`gamma < 0`) | 0 | 28 |
| `oddden` | thirds, fifths | 28 | 2-integral, odd denominators | holds on 28 | 0 | 28 |
| `mixed` | halves and thirds | 28 | general `Q` | fails on 28 (`gamma < 0`) | 0 | 28 |

84 instances, `v = 3..10`, zero falsifiers, 84 of 84 certified (minimum ratio 1.0; exact `cert = v` on all 36 decided instances, `v = 3..5`). 56 instances lie outside Lemma AN's literal hypothesis and were covered by Lemma SG's scaling; 66 of 84 have anchor reach below threshold and were carried by the coefficient-free matched-pivot or general-labelling certificate. The scope identity `K_ts = M_ts mod 2` was machine-checked on every instance. **Early kill with the exact obstruction recorded:** by pattern invariance the entry-class axis cannot produce a falsifier beyond the shared combinatorial `(pi, sigma, Z)` space, so the search was a regression test of the scope machinery; the falsifier criterion (admissible-B chain cost) was armed but never needed to fire. The true residual obstruction is exactly (i-prime) the cancellation lines `{t : v_2(M_tt) > gamma}` — now containing PR 2747's tied-minimum repair/ordering problem and Lemma AN's anchor-count axis — together with (ii) the zero digraphs of PR 2774. **Residue class (iii) is DEMOTED: mis-stated (odd primes in denominators are 2-integral and anchor-covered verbatim) and empty (entry-class-invariance). The residue classification is renamed to (i-prime) and (ii).**

## Claims ledger

- **PROVEN:** Lemma SC (with the `Z[1/2]` / `Z_(2)` / `Q` coverage and both directions of the criterion); Lemma SG (scale-invariant anchor, exact reach `S_gamma`, repaired AN corollary); pattern invariance (integer realization included); the Lemma MX / SF / MP / RK scope remark.
- **CHECKED:** controls 3/3 brute-force agreement, diagonal `cert = 3`, corrupted-witness rejection 2/2, MAS 3/3, chi 4/4, `MP = 3` diagonal control, and 4 scope controls (dyadic negative-content instance where AN's hypothesis fails and SG anchors everything; scaled `M = 2 I_3` with naive count 0 and reach 3; odd-denominator anchor verbatim; reach-witness replay); the fixture settlement and every calibration anchor above; the 84-instance search. Certificate digest `39f5c167c495f457`.
- **DEMOTED / OPEN:** class (iii) as stated; F-star for general rational decoders remains open; the fixture limits 11/18 rest on PR 2111's recorded CP-SAT optimality, not re-verified here; `chi(Z) >= 4` above `v = 13` remains budget-limited.
